title: Accenture Q4 Earnings Call Sees AI Demand Broaden Into FY27
author: Na
description: Accenture exceeded Q4 FY2026 earnings expectations with $3.29 EPS and $18.68B revenue, driven by broad-based demand across all markets and strong AI adoption. The company added nearly 100 first-time advanced AI clients in Q4, bringing the fiscal 2026 total above 400. For FY2027, Accenture projects 3-6% revenue growth in local currency while facing pricing pressure and cautious discretionary spending. The company plans $5B in acquisition spending and at least $9.5B in capital returns while maintaining margin expansion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Accenture beat both EPS and revenue estimates, demonstrated broad-based demand across all geographic markets and service lines, added 100+ new advanced AI clients, and projects continued growth despite headwinds. Strong AI momentum, planned acquisitions, and margin expansion support positive outlook, though guidance range reflects macro uncertainty and pricing pressure.

title: Can CDW Corporation Restore Margin Momentum in the Second Half?
author: Na
description: CDW reported solid Q2 2026 results with 10% YoY sales growth but faced 70 bps gross margin decline due to higher-mix hardware infrastructure and enterprise orders. The company expects operating leverage improvements in H2 2026 through efficiency initiatives. Competitors ServiceNow, Accenture, and Avnet also face margin pressures from AI adoption and infrastructure costs, though some show stabilization efforts.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with strong revenue growth (10% YoY) and EPS increase (12%), but offset by significant gross margin decline (70 bps) due to unfavorable product mix. Management expects improvement in H2 2026, suggesting cautious optimism.

Gross margins declined significantly (total margin down 300 bps to 78%, subscription margin down 250 bps to 80.5%) due to AI adoption and hyperscaler infrastructure costs, despite stable operating margins and management's cost-offset initiatives.

Operating income increased 6% YoY with operating margin expansion of 20 bps to 17%, supported by strong Managed Services growth and disciplined cost management despite ongoing AI and labor-related cost pressures.

Adjusted operating margin expanded significantly (129 bps YoY to 3.8%), with Farnell margin reaching 9% and management targeting double-digit margins by end of fiscal 2027, indicating improving profitability trajectory.

title: Company News for Oct 2, 2026
author: Na
description: Several major companies reported quarterly earnings with mixed results. Accenture surged 15.8% after beating earnings estimates, while McKesson gained 5.3% on maintained guidance. Conversely, Acuity fell 3.4% and Progress Software dropped 8.5% after missing revenue expectations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company beat consensus earnings estimate ($3.29 vs $3.19 expected), resulting in a 15.8% share price increase
Company missed revenue consensus estimate ($1,244.40M vs $1,251.87M expected), causing a 3.4% share price decline
Company reiterated fiscal 2027 earnings guidance, demonstrating confidence and resulting in a 5.3% share price increase
Company missed revenue consensus estimate ($246.01M vs $247.16M expected), leading to an 8.5% share price decline

title: Why Did Infosys Stock Pop on Thursday?
author: Rich Smith
description: Infosys stock jumped 6.6% on Thursday following Accenture's strong Q4 earnings beat, which exceeded analyst expectations on both revenue ($18.7B vs $18B expected) and earnings ($3.29 vs $3.19 EPS expected). Investors are extrapolating Accenture's positive results to anticipate similar strong performance from Infosys when it reports earnings on October 23. However, the author notes Infosys faces a high bar for sales growth (10.7% expected) and a low bar for earnings growth (5% expected), requiring significantly faster earnings growth to be considered a buy.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Accenture beat analyst expectations on both revenue and earnings, reported 6% sales growth, 370 basis points of operating margin improvement, and 46% increase in net income. Provided guidance for FY2027 with 3-6% sales growth and 6-9% earnings growth, demonstrating strong operational performance.

Stock gained 6.6% based on positive sentiment from Accenture's results rather than its own fundamentals. While the stock appears cheaper at 13.3x trailing earnings versus Accenture's 14.7x, the author expresses skepticism about whether Infosys can meet expectations, noting that 5% earnings growth is insufficient for a buy recommendation despite high sales growth expectations of 10.7%.

title: Accenture's Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Increase 6% Y/Y
author: Na
description: Accenture delivered impressive Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings of $3.29 per share (up 8.6% YoY) and revenues of $18.7B (up 6.2% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. The company projects FY27 local-currency revenue growth of 3-6% with EPS of $14.39-$14.81. Managed Services bookings led at $12.77B, and the company expanded operating margins to 15.3%. FactSet Research and Paychex also reported strong quarterly results.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Beat earnings and revenue consensus estimates, demonstrated broad-based growth across work types and geographies, expanded operating margins, strong bookings of $22.17B with 1.2 book-to-bill ratio, and raised dividend by 5%. However, FY27 guidance midpoint slightly below consensus and free cash flow declined YoY.
Reported adjusted earnings of $4.52 per share, beating consensus by 4.6% with 11.6% YoY growth. Revenues of $634.7M topped consensus and grew 6.3% YoY.
Posted adjusted earnings of $1.34 per share, up 9.8% YoY and beating consensus estimate. Total revenues rose 5.9% to $1.63B, exceeding consensus mark.
